title: Producer-supplied acceptance-check specification
description: Declared by the worker that produced an artifact, as part of that artifact's deliverable set. FINPRODLINE_PROTOCOL.md §2.6. This is DATA: Terminal evaluates it with the single generic evaluator (scripts/fpl_validate.py) and never executes returned code. Declaring checks is not auditing — §5.4 passage still requires an independent integrated audit verdict, and the audit assesses these checks for coverage, strength and independence rather than trusting them.

request_id.description: The commission this specification belongs to. Must agree with the call's request_id.

produced_by_worker.description: The worker id that produced the artifacts being checked.

targets.description: The artifacts this specification covers, with identity. Declaring them here does not check them; declare file_hash / file_size checks for that.

criteria.description: The acceptance criteria this artifact was commissioned against. Every criterion must be declared here, and the evaluator enforces coverage: a criterion with disposition mechanical or partial must be named in at least one check's `proves`; a criterion with disposition semantic_only must NOT be, and must state a reason. Declaring `criteria` is required as soon as any check uses `proves` — otherwise coverage cannot be verified and the specification is refused. The earlier contract forced every declared criterion to be claimed as mechanically proved, which made an honest declaration impossible for criteria no check can establish; disposition fixes that.

source.description: Where the criterion came from: the directive id, plan, or protocol section.

disposition.description: mechanical: declared checks fully establish it. partial: checks establish bounded mechanical evidence only. semantic_only: no mechanical check can establish it — this is a legitimate and expected answer, and it must state a reason.

reason.description: Required when disposition is semantic_only: why no mechanical check can establish this criterion. Honesty here is worth more than a vacuous check.

beyond_mechanical.description: What an independent audit must still establish, when disposition is partial or semantic_only.

type.description: The declared check type. Types are supplied by Terminal's generic evaluator; a producer may not invent one. If no type expresses a wanted check, the specification is restated, not the evaluator extended.

target.description: A plain basename inside the return's artifact set.

message.description: What a failure of this check means.

pointer.description: RFC 6901 JSON pointer, for the json_* types.

value.description: Expected value, for json_equals / json_type / numeric_close.

explode.description: Treat each item's array value as contributing values, for json_array_covers.

id_key.description: Node id field, for the dependency and graph types.

dependencies_key.description: Dependency field, for the dependency and graph types.

actor_pattern.description: Regex the actor must satisfy, for jsonl_hash_chain.

exclude_fields.description: Fields removed in addition to hash_field before the event hash is recomputed. Defaults to event_id, which is required: STATE_PROTOCOL.md 2.2 derives event_id from event_hash, so event_id is computed last and is not itself hashed. Omitting it would fail every valid ledger.

notes.description: Anything the producer wants the reader to know about these checks, including what they deliberately do not cover.
